text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
24 CHASA

-- Bulgaria may change amendments in its constitution to allow investors from European Union (EU) countries to buy land in the country in a move to meet requirements for Bulgaria's integration in the EU, said Union of Democratic Forces deputy Ekaterina Michailova.
-- Bulgaria's June monthly inflation is expected to slow down to under five percent from 5.6 percent in May, statistics experts said.
-- Bulgaria is expected to raise central heating charges by 12 percent from Tuesday, Energy Committee chairman Georgi Stoilov said in an interview for the state national radio.
TRUD

-- Bulgaria's police said it had cracked down two gatherings of disciples of Moon's Unification Church in Bulgaria's southern cities of Plovdiv and Asenovgrad. Visiting preachers from Korea, Japan and the Czech Republic were arrested, books and videotapes were confiscated.
STANDART
-- Bulgarian army officers said they had seen an Unidentified Flying Object (UFO) in the sky near Bulgaria's western town of Sliven on Sunday. Army experts are expected to investigate the incident.
-- Bulgaria is expected to raise the minimal pension to 27,000 levs from 24,300 levs from tomorrow, the National Social Insurance Institute said.

-- Bulgaria is expected to organise an international meeting on money laundry in a bid to boost intergovernment cooperation against "white collar" crime in the post-communist countries, Prime minister Ivan Kostov said.
-- Bulgaria plans some $268 million foreign debt payments in the third quarter of this year, Finance ministry officials said.
-- Bulgaria is expected to raise electricity charges by 6.8 percent from tomorrow, Energy Committee chairman Georgi Stoilov said.
PARI
-- Bulgaria's broad money rose by 115 billion levs in the trird week of June to 3.971 trillion levs, Bulgarian National Bank figures showed.

-- Bulgaria's deputy George Ganchev, elected on the ticket of the Bulgarian Business Bloc, said he had discussed with Russia's MAPO airplane producer a possible deal to buy MiG-29 jetfighters under a 15 year credit agreement with five years grace period.
-- Bulgaria's State Savings Bank is expected to extend some 150 billion levs to fund purchasing of wheat from this year's crop, Agriculture minister Ventsislav Varbanov said.
-- Bulgarian cars and fuel sales fell by 68 percent in the first quarter of this year compared to the same period in 1996, National Statistics Institute figures showed.
NOVINAR

-- Bulgaria's police said it had seized 540 tonnes of washing powder, soaps and cosmetics illegaly imported in the country from Turkey in Bulgaria's southeast town of Aitos. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
